text:
devin-se: Hey team — noticed my net pay this cycle was ~20% lower than usual. I think state tax withholding changed after my move in Sept. Can someone confirm what withholding state was applied?

mike-payroll: @devin-se I can check. Quick Qs: what’s the address we have on file and the date you changed residence?

devin-se: Moved from OR to WA on 2025-09-14. My profile in Workday shows WA address but I remember submitting a change request mid-Oct. Pay stub attached here (redacted):

devin-se: ```
Gross: $9,600.00
Federal: $1,440.00
State: $1,920.00
Other deductions: $200.00
Net: $5,— (redacted)
```

payroll-bot: Automated payroll run: payroll-2026-03 completed. If you believe state withholding is incorrect, please file a ticket: #payroll-ticket and include your last pay stub and move date.

mike-payroll: Thanks @devin-se. From the stub it looks like OR withholding rates were applied (OR withheld ~20% on that line). WA has no state income tax so you should not have had state withholding post-move. Two possibilities: payroll ran with your old state because the HR address update happened after the cut-off, or we didn’t receive a state withholding form for WA (some states require a change form).

sara-finance: If it was incorrectly withheld, we can do a retroactive payroll adjustment or refund via an off-cycle payment. Alternatively the employee can claim a refund when filing the OR state return for that tax year. We usually prefer adjusting payroll when the error is clearly on our side and documentation is provided.

ashley-hr: @devin-se please confirm you updated your address in Workday and -- if you changed your withholding elections -- that you submitted a state form (OR Form OR-W-4 or WA equivalent). Also confirm your official start date in WA for benefits/insurance eligibility — just to make sure all systems are aligned.

devin-se: Confirmed I updated Workday on 2025-10-02. I did NOT submit any OR withholding form after the move; didn’t realize I needed to. I thought WA had no state tax so nothing to do.

mike-payroll: Ok — that explains it. Payroll cut-off for the Oct run was 2025-10-01 so your update missed that cycle. Since Workday shows WA now, future runs should be correct. For the withheld OR amount we need: 1) copy of the pay stub (you pasted redacted) 2) the Workday change audit (we can pull it) 3) confirmation of move date. Once ticket is in I’ll route to adjustments queue.

devin-se: Filing ticket now — #payroll-ticket/1713912345. Included stub and move date.

mike-payroll: Got it. I’ll review and flag for an off-cycle adjustment. Two notes: 1) If we issue a refund via payroll it will be taxed for FICA/Medicare again unless processed as a corrective adjustment — we’ll aim for a corrective tax adjustment so net refund is right. 2) For W-2: if the withholding belongs to OR we might need to issue a corrected W-2c for the tax year if the annual totals change. We’ll coordinate with you before issuing any W-2c.

sara-finance: If the refund is processed this FY, tax reporting needs to reflect the correction in our payroll system. Sometimes we offset in a subsequent pay run if small, or create a dedicated adjustment record for visibility. Mike will advise exact flow after review.

ashley-hr: Also remind folks: when changing states mid-year, please submit the state withholding form (OR-W4, CA DE 4, etc.) even if your new state has no income tax — it helps payroll reconcile addresses. We’re updating the handbook blurb to make this clearer. :memo:

devin-se: Appreciate it. One more Q — will this affect my benefits premiums or retirement deferrals?

mike-payroll: Generally no for retirement deferrals (401k is pre-tax federal and FICA unaffected). Benefit premium allocations can be state-sensitive only for certain local taxes; looks like nothing changed for you. I’ll flag if anything else pops up.

payroll-bot: Ticket #payroll-ticket/1713912345 assigned to mike-payroll. Status: triage.

mike-payroll: Follow-up: processed a corrective adjustment for the Oct–Dec 2025 period. You’ll see an off-cycle payment next Friday with a net refund. I’ve put a note that a W-2c may be required; if so HR will contact you to confirm mailing address before we issue.

devin-se: Thank you! :relieved:

ashley-hr: Thanks @mike-payroll and @sara-finance for the quick turnaround. Adding a reminder to the new-hire checklist for multi-state moves.

mike-payroll: Closing loop: Devin, please verify the off-cycle when it hits and reply in ticket if amounts look off; we’ll run a final reconciliation and confirm W-2 status by end of month.

devin-se: Will do. Thanks everyone.
